title: FlowX onboarding spec (v2)
description: Mirrors src/flowx/lakeflow_framework/onboarding/spec_validator.py as closely as JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) allows. See onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec_full_reference.md for a field-by-field walkthrough and onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec_full_reference.json for a fully-populated example that validates against this schema.
$comment: Known gaps this schema CANNOT express (spec_validator.py enforces all of these at onboarding time; a schema-valid document can still fail real validation for one of these reasons): (1) transformation_flows[].source_inputs[].input_name must be unique across the WHOLE spec, not just within one flow -- a cross-array-element uniqueness constraint JSON Schema has no keyword for. (2) transformation_sql / reconciliation transform_sql are syntax- and plan-validated live via `EXPLAIN <sql>` against a real Spark session -- this schema only checks they are non-empty strings. (3) decrypted_columns[].cast_to_type is cross-checked at RUNTIME (not onboarding time) against a Unity Catalog `original_data_type` column tag captured when the column was encrypted -- not checkable from the spec document alone. The same is true of encrypted_columns[].source_data_type, which is compared at encryption time against the type Spark actually reports for the column; this schema can only check it is a non-empty string. (4) source_config.schema_location, when omitted for source_type in {autoloader, asn1}, is auto-derived from target_catalog/target_table by the loader before this required-field check ever runs -- so an onboarding attempt with schema_location omitted is NOT actually an error in practice, even though this schema (matching the validator's own literal required-field check on the object as originally supplied) marks it required. (5) data_standardization_sql entries are checked against a forbidden-keyword regex (no bare SELECT/FROM/JOIN/UNION/WHERE/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/GRANT/REVOKE, no ';') and must end in `AS <column>` -- expressible only as a loose pattern here, not the exact semantic check. (6) sink_config.write_mode is accepted by the validator (any key validates as long as the parent is an object) but is dead code -- never read by the engine; kept here as a documented-but-inert enum for fidelity with the ALLOWED_SINK_WRITE_MODES constant that exists in spec_validator.py. (7) This schema requires source_config on every ingestion_flows entry (per its source_type), but _validate_ingestion_source_config actually no-ops and reports nothing when source_config itself is entirely absent (None) -- so a spec omitting source_config outright currently passes real onboarding validation even though it is schema-invalid here; this schema intentionally takes the stricter, more useful stance for a spec author. (8) reconciliation_flows[].target_configs[].target_id must be unique within its own flow (_validate_reconciliation_target_configs) -- the same class of cross-array-element uniqueness constraint as (1), which JSON Schema has no keyword for. (9) source_zip_handling.delete_source_after_extract's object form accepts `days` alongside `action: 'delete_now'` here (it is simply an unused property), but _validate_delete_source_after_extract rejects that combination -- a `days` that would be silently inert reads as a working configuration and is not one. (10) source_config.dedup_watermark validates on its own here, but the validator rejects it unless remove_dups is also true: on its own it configures nothing, and accepting it silently would let an author believe dedup was enabled when it was not. (11) source_config.json_string_columns[].column must be unique across the array (the second entry would silently overwrite the first's parse) -- the same cross-array-element uniqueness class as (1). (12) The v1.4.0 REMOVED attributes -- source_config.normalize_column_names, target_config.generate_surrogate_key/surrogate_key_columns/surrogate_key_exclude_columns, reconciliation_flows[].recon_mode/generate_surrogate_key -- are absent from this schema but are not rejected by it, because every object carrying them sets additionalProperties: true (deliberately, so a forward-compatible spec is not broken by an older schema copy). spec_validator.py rejects each one by name with a migration message; a document still carrying them is schema-valid here and will still fail onboarding. (13) source_config.landing_retention_policy is rejected outright for source_type 'zerobus' (a Delta-table stream has no landing zone to clean); expressible as a conditional here but deliberately left to the validator so the reason travels with the error message. (14) observability[].destination_config.event_log_tables is rejected on a 'triggered' destination (the triggered engine resolves its pipeline from the upstream task run, so the list would be silently ignored) -- this schema only enforces the converse, that a 'continuous' destination must supply it. (15) reconciliation_flows[].source_config/target_configs[].read_mode 'streaming' is rejected only when the OWNING FLOW's execution_mode is 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only' -- a cross-field conditional on a SIBLING field of a DIFFERENT object (the flow, not the dataset side) this schema does not encode; read_mode's own enum here stays {batch, streaming} regardless of execution_mode. The same cross-field conditional applies to source_config/target_configs[].task_run_id_column (rejected on presence, not value, in pipeline modes) and to the flow-level publish_schema/dq_config (rejected on presence while execution_mode is still 'job', the default) -- see reject_mode_incompatible_keys in spec_validator.py. (16) reconciliation_flows[].dq_config.rules[].action accepts the full dqRule action enum here (warn/drop/fail/quarantine -- the same $ref as ingestion/transformation dq_config), but the validator rejects 'quarantine' specifically for a reconciliation flow, since there is nothing to quarantine on the one-row __metrics dataset these rules attach to. (17) reconciliation_flows[].dataflow_group_id is required only when this same flow's own execution_mode is 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only' -- another cross-field conditional requirement; the property itself is always optional here. (18) reconciliation_flows[].source_config.table and target_configs[].append_target_table participate in several cross-array-element identity checks against ingestion_flows[]/transformation_flows[] targets and zerobus ingestion sources (_validate_reconciliation_pipeline_placement) -- e.g. append_target_table must not equal any in-spec target, any in-spec ingestion source in the same dataflow group, this flow's own source_config.table, or any of its own target_configs[].table; and a pipeline-mode source_config.table must resolve to a target this same dataflow group actually produces. Every one of these is a cross-array-element, casefolded three-part table-name comparison, the same constraint class as (1) and (8), which JSON Schema has no keyword for. (19) A pipeline-mode reconciliation source that resolves to a producer whose cdc_load_strategy dispatches through dlt.apply_changes[_from_snapshot] (SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC), or to TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD into a materialized_view, is rejected -- execution_mode 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only' requires an append-only producer, pointing an author at execution_mode 'job' instead. This depends on a DIFFERENT array element's cdc_load_strategy/target_type than the reconciliation flow being validated, so it cannot be expressed here either. (20) More than one distinct source_config.landing_retention_policy or source_zip_handling across ingestion_flows[] entries that share the same source_config.path is rejected -- cloudFiles.cleanSource and PGP/zip extraction are both destructive, path-scoped side effects, so two different regimes on one shared directory is a data-loss race, not two independent settings. The same cross-array-element constraint class as (18).

pipeline_parameters.description: Runtime parameters substituted into ${param} placeholders. Values may be any JSON type -- rendered via str() at substitution time (strings are single-quoted; everything else is not).

spark_config.description: Group-scoped Spark configuration applied to the pipeline session before any flow is registered. Precedence, lowest to highest: engine/spark_config.py's FRAMEWORK_SPARK_DEFAULTS < this block < the pipeline resource's own `configuration: dataflow.spark.conf` JSON object. Values are rendered with str() (booleans as lowercase true/false) before spark.conf.set. Distinct from pipeline_parameters, which is ${param} string substitution, not Spark configuration.

source_plane.description: The read-once threshold policy for this dataflow group's Lakeflow pipeline -- see the CANONICAL IDENTITY / SHARING RULES sections of docs/13 and engine/source_plane.py. Persisted to the new nullable dataflow_group_spec.source_plane_config_json column via onboarding/metadata_upsert.py (json.dumps(spec.get('source_plane', {}))); read back via getattr(GROUP_ROW, 'source_plane_config_json', None), so an existing control-table row predating this column reads as {} (all defaults).

observability.description: Telemetry destinations for the DLT observability engine, scoped to this dataflow_group_id (see docs/25_dlt_observability_module.md). Upserted into observability_config by onboarding/metadata_upsert.py::upsert_observability_config alongside every other control table from this same spec -- no separate observability config file.

$schema.description: Editor hint; ignored by the framework.

secretRef.description: Unity Catalog three-level secret reference, resolved via dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=). Used identically for every encryption/decryption key, ZIP password, PGP key, and Kafka sink credential in the framework.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.
Author comment; ignored by the framework.

quarantine_table.description: Default: '<target_table>_quarantine'. Only ever materialized when >=1 rule has action=quarantine.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

sourcePlane.description: Top-level dataflow_group_spec.source_plane -- see the top-level source_plane property. additionalProperties is deliberately false: unlike most $defs in this schema, there is no forward-compatibility reason to accept an unknown key here, since this whole block is new in v1.5.0.

materialize.description: 'always' (default, and the only policy since v1.7.3's Single-Read architectural mandate): every external physical read locator is materialized into its own L0 base node regardless of fanout, so N distinct source tables produce N base ingestion nodes and every consumer binds to one via dlt.read()/dlt.read_stream() instead of re-reading the origin. 'auto' is the retained LEGACY policy and is genuinely distinct, not an alias: it materializes an external identity only at fanout >= 2 within this pipeline update and leaves a single-consumer identity inline (re-read inside that consumer's own closure). Fanout is counted per (identity, execution mode), so a locator consumed once as a stream and once as a batch is fanout 1 in EACH mode, not fanout 2 -- those two consumers can never share one node anyway, since a materialized view cannot be read with dlt.read_stream. Use it only to keep a group onboarded before v1.7.3 on the DAG topology it was onboarded with; it is a strictly weaker guarantee than 'always' and is not recommended for new specs. 'never' was REMOVED in v1.7.3 and is now hard-rejected at onboarding time by spec_validator.py (_validate_source_plane) with a migration message, and again at plan time by engine/source_plane.py::plan_source_plane for control-table rows persisted before the mandate. Note that read-once means once per source PER EXECUTION MODE: streaming and batch nodes stay distinct (the __stream/__batch node-name suffix), because a batch-bound materialized view cannot be read as a stream.

catalog.description: Catalog for PUBLISHED L0 source-plane nodes (the `_src__<sanitized_locator>__<8hex>__stream`/`__batch` datasets). Since v1.6.0 the default (null) means the node is NOT published at all: it is registered as a pipeline-scoped temporary table -- still materialized once (read-once holds) but never visible in Unity Catalog (the Intermediate Object Rule). Set catalog AND schema together only when you deliberately want the shared node published as a durable, queryable table. Pre-v1.6.0, null meant 'publish into the hosting pipeline's own catalog/schema'.

schema.description: Schema for PUBLISHED L0 source-plane nodes. Since v1.6.0 the default (null) means the node stays a pipeline-scoped temporary table (not published); set catalog AND schema together to publish. Pre-v1.6.0, null meant the hosting pipeline's own schema.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

governanceTags.description: Tags-only model -- applies key/value Unity Catalog tags; does not create/administer the mask/row-filter policy a tag activates.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

enable_iceberg_read_uniformity.description: Enables Iceberg read access (Delta UniForm). The emitted properties depend on target_type: a batch_table gets IcebergCompatV2 (columnMapping.mode=name, enableIcebergCompatV2, universalFormat.enabledFormats=iceberg); a pipeline-managed streaming_table/materialized_view gets IcebergCompatV3 instead (columnMapping.mode=name, enableIcebergCompatV3, enableRowTracking, pipelines.externalMetadata.enabled, universalFormat.enabledFormats=iceberg), because Databricks does not support IcebergCompatV2 on those types at all. NOTE: IcebergCompatV3 is mutually exclusive with Change Data Feed, so on a CDC-dispatched flow delta.enableChangeDataFeed is SUPPRESSED (logged at WARNING) and post-deployment SCD change-count capture will not work for that target. Valid for ANY target_type, unlike storage_format:'iceberg' which is batch_table-only.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

autoTtl.description: Opt-in and individually forgiving: supplying only one of the two sub-fields (or neither) is not an error -- Auto TTL is simply not applied. Only takes effect for cdc_load_strategy in {APPEND, TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD} -- a fully-populated block on any other strategy is a hard onboarding error (see the parent targetConfig's allOf rule).

encryptedColumn.description: target_config.encrypted_columns[] -- SQL OUTPUT column encryption only.

source_data_type.description: Optional (v1.4.0). The original source data type of column_name, before encryption replaces it with ciphertext binary -- e.g. 'string', 'decimal(18,2)', 'timestamp'. Captured as the Unity Catalog original_data_type column tag, which is what a downstream source_inputs[].decrypted_columns[].cast_to_type is validated against. OMITTING IT IS SAFE: the framework falls back to the type Spark reports for the column at encryption time, which is the pre-v1.4.0 behaviour. Declaring it turns a silent source type change into a loud failure at encryption time (declared vs observed are compared case-insensitively; a mismatch raises).

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

decryptedColumn.description: source_inputs[].decrypted_columns[] -- the ONLY valid place to decrypt a SOURCE column.

mode.description: Default: GCM. Must match the mode the column was originally encrypted with.

cast_to_type.description: Required -- decryption may change the physical column type. Any Spark SQL type name.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

landingRetentionPolicy.description: Auto Loader landing-zone cleanup (cloudFiles.cleanSource) for source_type in {autoloader, asn1} only -- a zerobus flow streams an existing Delta table and has no landing zone, so a policy there is a hard onboarding error. archive_path is NEVER required: see its own description. See ingestion/readers.py::resolve_landing_retention_policy.

clean_source.description: Default: 'off'. Maps to cloudFiles.cleanSource. Auto Loader file ingestion only -- never applied to the source_zip_handling pre-extraction path.

archive_path.description: Optional even for clean_source == 'archive'. An empty/absent archive_path with clean_source == 'archive' degrades to 'off' (no retention or cleanup action at all) with a WARNING log -- it is never an error. Ignored entirely for clean_source == 'delete'.

retention_days.description: Default: 7. 0 is valid and distinct from omitting the field: it means NO age threshold at all -- a file becomes eligible for archive/delete as soon as Auto Loader has committed it (cloudFiles.cleanSource.retentionDuration = '0 days'). Omitting the field means 7 days, not 0.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

preExtractionDecryption.description: Fully optional at every level -- absent, or {}, means a plain, unencrypted, non-password-protected ZIP. 'type' (an outer whole-file decryption layer, e.g. PGP) and 'secret_passphrase' (the ZIP archive's own AES password) are independently optional and combinable: decrypt the envelope via 'type', then extract the password-protected ZIP it contained via 'secret_passphrase'. For member_format 'gzip', 'secret_passphrase' is rejected -- a gzip stream has no archive password.

type.description: Type-dispatched registry. 'pgp' is key-based (asymmetric) and requires private_key_secret; 'pgp_symmetric' (v1.7.4) is passphrase-based -- the shape `gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256` produces -- and requires passphrase_secret instead. The two are mutually exclusive at the OpenPGP message level, so a message encrypted one way cannot be decrypted the other. Omit entirely when there is no outer decryption layer.

passphrase_secret.description: Required when type == 'pgp_symmetric' (the shared passphrase IS the key). Optional when type == 'pgp', where it only unlocks a passphrase-protected private key.

secret_passphrase.description: AES password on the ZIP archive itself -- independent of 'type'. Omit for a plain, unprotected ZIP.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

sourceZipHandling.description: Shared by source_type in {autoloader, asn1} -- not applicable to zerobus (no landing-zone file to unzip). source_zip_path is a landing DIRECTORY, never a single file. member_format selects the container (zip/gzip), orthogonally to any decryption layer.

zip_file_pattern.description: Required when enabled. A glob, e.g. 'orders_*.zip'.

member_format.description: Default 'zip' (the only pre-v1.7.4 behaviour): a real archive with N named members, opened by pyzipper. 'gzip' (v1.7.4) is a single compressed stream with no member table, which pyzipper cannot open at all. Note an UNENCRYPTED .gz needs no source_zip_handling whatsoever -- Spark's codec layer decompresses it transparently on read; 'gzip' is for the encrypted case (e.g. .csv.gz.gpg), where the file must be decrypted to disk first and what remains is a bare gzip stream. The landed filename has its .gz plus any .gpg/.pgp envelope suffix stripped, since that landed name is what file_pattern matches.

delete_source_after_extract.description: Default: {"action": "delete_now"}. Accepts the legacy plain boolean (true == delete_now, false == never) for backward compatibility. delete_after_x_days does not delete an archive as part of extracting it -- it runs an age-based sweep of source_zip_path at extraction time, removing every archive matching zip_file_pattern whose modification time is older than `days` days, except any archive whose extraction failed in that same run (so a failed extraction is never swept out from under a retry).

pre_extraction_decryption.description: Optional -- absent or {} means a plain, unencrypted ZIP. See preExtractionDecryption.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

passphrase_secret.description: v1.7.4. Symmetric (passphrase) encryption -- the shape `gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256` produces. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with recipient_public_key_secret: a PGP message is encrypted either to a recipient key or under a shared passphrase, never both. Signing (sign_with_private_key_secret) requires a sender keypair and is not available for symmetric encryption.

allOf.$comment: v1.7.4: exactly one of recipient_public_key_secret (asymmetric, encrypt to a recipient's key) or passphrase_secret (symmetric, encrypt under a shared passphrase). A PGP message is one or the other, never both, and _validate_sink_config states the same rule with a clearer message. Before v1.7.4 the recipient key was unconditionally required, which is why symmetric encryption was unreachable from a spec at all.
_validate_sink_config hard-errors when sign_passphrase_secret is set without sign_with_private_key_secret -- 'only meaningful alongside a signing key'.
Signing requires a sender keypair, so it has no meaning for symmetric encryption.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

enabled.description: Must be true for sink_config.format == 'pgp_zip' -- archiving IS what that sink format does.

output_zip_path.description: Required when enabled. One finished archive file per micro-batch.

archive_format.description: v1.7.4. Default 'zip' (unchanged): an AES-capable ZIP holding one file per staged partition. 'gzip' concatenates this micro-batch's staged files into a single gzip stream (a gzip holds exactly one member) and names the export '<export_file_name_format>.<csv|jsonl>.gz', or '....gz.gpg' when pgp_encryption is enabled. Note 'secret' (an AES password on a ZIP) has no meaning for 'gzip'.

export_file_name_format.description: Optional str.format()-style template for the exported archive's own file name, e.g. '{timestamp}_{batch_id}_export.zip'.

secret.description: Optional AES password on the ZIP itself -- independent of, and combinable with, pgp_encryption.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

sinkConfig.description: Required on target_config when the flow's target_type is 'sink' or 'external_sink'.

staged_file_format.description: v1.6.0, 'pgp_zip' only (presence-rejected for 'delta'/'kafka', which have no framework staging step): the staged per-partition file format inside the archive. 'json' (default when absent -- JSON-Lines, the only pre-v1.6.0 behaviour) or 'csv' (RFC-4180 with a header row; one staged file per non-empty partition per micro-batch, header order = the sink's write schema). See archive/pgp_zip_sink.py.

export_trigger.description: v1.7.5, 'pgp_zip' only (presence-rejected for 'delta'/'kafka', whose write cadence Lakeflow itself owns): WHAT drives the export. 'per_micro_batch' (default when absent -- the only pre-v1.7.5 behaviour) feeds the sink from the flow's own staged view, producing one archive per micro-batch of an append-only stream. 'per_update' decouples trigger from payload: an update-scoped pulse drives the sink and the rows are read batch-side, producing exactly ONE export per pipeline update -- including an update that ingested no new rows. 'per_update' is what makes an aggregating materialized_view / TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD target exportable at all: such a target is fully recomputed each update, which Delta refuses to stream from (DELTA_SOURCE_TABLE_IGNORE_CHANGES), so before v1.7.5 it had no sink path. See engine/sink_registration.py.

staged_file_options.description: v1.7.4. The staged CSV's dialect -- only valid alongside staged_file_format 'csv' (JSON-Lines has no delimiter or header). Before this, the writer used Python's csv `excel` default: comma-separated, always headered, CRLF-terminated, with no way to express a supplier interface that specifies otherwise.

include_header.description: Default true. False emits data rows only.

line_terminator.description: Default 'crlf' (RFC 4180, and the pre-v1.7.4 behaviour). 'lf' for an interface specifying a bare LF record delimiter. Spelled as a name because a JSON string cannot carry a bare control character unambiguously.

kafka_options.description: Required for 'kafka'. _validate_sink_config hard-errors if either 'kafka.bootstrap.servers' or 'topic' is missing/falsy -- expressed here as a real required-keys constraint, not just descriptive text.

kafka_secret_options.description: Framework-specific: a connector option whose literal value must embed a resolved secret.

write_mode.$comment: Dead field: validates fine (ALLOWED_SINK_WRITE_MODES exists in spec_validator.py) but is never read by the engine's 'delta' sink branch. @dlt.append_flow is always append-only. Kept here only for fidelity with the validator's own constant; omit it in real specs.

post_export_archive.description: Required (and enabled must be true) when format == 'pgp_zip'. Structurally accepted, but unused, for 'delta'/'kafka' if a spec author supplies it anyway.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

targetConfig.description: Shared, field-for-field identical shape between ingestion_flows[] and transformation_flows[]. Every CDC-related field lives directly inside target_config -- there is no separate cdc_config sibling.

storage_format.description: Default: 'delta'. 'iceberg' only valid when the enclosing flow's target_type == 'batch_table' (enforced at the flow level, not here).

partition_columns.description: Only takes effect for cdc_load_strategy in {APPEND, TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD}. An explicitly empty array ([]) is valid and means NO partitioning -- it is never an error and is behaviourally identical to omitting the field.

liquid_clustering_columns.description: At most 3 columns (Delta Liquid Clustering's own limit). Same APPEND/TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD-only caveat as partition_columns. An explicitly empty array is valid and means no clustering.

cdc_load_strategy.description: Superset of both flow kinds' allowed values. SCD3 is transformation_flows-only -- a hard error on any ingestion_flows entry (enforced at the ingestionFlow level, not here). FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK was REMOVED in v1.4.0 with the surrogate-key engine: snapshot CDC now requires real primary_keys (the Databricks-native apply_changes_from_snapshot pattern, https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/cdc), or TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD for a source with no key.

primary_keys.description: Required for cdc_load_strategy in {SCD1, SCD2, SCD3, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC}.

sequence_by_column.description: Optional for SCD1/SCD2/SCD3 -- falls back to __framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc.

columns_to_check.description: Comparison-scoping; empty/absent = compare every applicable column. Never include an encrypted (GCM) column here.

columns_to_exclude.description: Only meaningful for cdc_load_strategy in {SCD1, SCD2, SCD3} -- flagged as a hard error otherwise.

cdc_operation_column.description: Only meaningful for cdc_load_strategy in {SCD1, SCD2, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC}. Required together with cdc_operation_mapping.

generate_hash_columns.description: Default: true for any CDC-dispatched strategy.

empty_target_if_source_empty.description: TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD only. Default: false -- a zero-record source NEVER blanks the target; the previously-materialized contents are preserved and the run logs why. Set true to allow an empty source to truncate the target to empty (the pre-v1.3.0 unconditional behaviour).

capture_technical_metadata.description: Conventionally transformation_flows-only (ingestion carries the equivalent field on source_config instead); not actually restricted by the validator.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

input_name.$comment: Must be unique across EVERY transformation_flows entry in the whole spec, not just within one flow -- a cross-array constraint this schema cannot express; see the top-level $comment.

table.description: Fully-qualified catalog.schema.table -- any table, not restricted to this spec's own ingestion_flows output.

watermark.description: Required when this streaming input is range-joined against another stream.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

items.description: A single column-expression string ending 'AS <column_name>' (e.g. "trim(customer_name) AS customer_name") -- never a full SELECT/FROM/JOIN/UNION or any DDL/DML statement, and never containing ';'.

ingestionSourceConfig.description: Shape depends on the sibling source_type -- see the ingestionFlow-level allOf for the per-source_type required fields.

explode_columns.description: PRESENT but EMPTY ([]) means auto-flatten ALL nested JSON columns (equivalent to auto_flatten_all: true). ABSENT (or null) means schema-preserving pass-through -- nothing is exploded or flattened. A populated list scopes struct-flatten/array-explode to exactly those top-level columns. This absent-vs-empty distinction is load-bearing: it is what prevents silent cartesian row explosion on un-configured sources.

json_string_columns.description: Columns holding a JSON document as a STRING. Each is parsed with from_json into a struct immediately before explode_columns/auto-flatten runs, so a Parquet (or CSV/Delta) source with embedded JSON text gets the same struct-flatten/array-explode treatment as a native JSON source. Supply schema_ddl whenever possible -- without it the framework falls back to Databricks' inferring from_json, which requires a streaming source with a checkpoint. See ingestion/json_flattening.py.

auto_flatten_all.description: Default: false. Opt-in -- only takes effect when explode_columns is empty/absent, in which case it switches from the default schema-preserving pass-through to recursively flattening every struct column and exploding every array column found anywhere in the schema. Ignored once explode_columns is populated. An explicitly-empty explode_columns ([]) already implies this. See ingestion/json_flattening.py.

remove_dups.description: Default: false. When true, apply full-row deduplication across the streaming dataset via dropDuplicates over every column EXCEPT the __framework_* technical columns and _rescued_data/_metadata/_object_metadata/_asn1_decode_error. Runs after explode/auto-flatten and before data_standardization_sql. WARNING: on a streaming source with no dedup_watermark this keeps unbounded state -- see ingestion/dedup.py.

dedup_watermark.description: Only meaningful alongside remove_dups: true on a streaming source. Bounds dedup state via withWatermark(...).dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark(...). Omit to accept unbounded dedup state.

event_time_column.description: A TIMESTAMP column on the ingested DataFrame.

delay_threshold.description: A Spark interval string, e.g. '2 hours', '30 minutes'.

format.description: autoloader only -- any cloudFiles.format value ('csv', 'parquet', 'json', 'avro', 'text', ...), not itself enum-restricted.

schema_location.description: autoloader/asn1 only. Auto-derived from target_catalog/target_table when omitted -- see the top-level $comment.

asn1_schema_path.description: asn1 only -- a real .asn module file.

asn1_pdu_name.description: asn1 only -- the top-level SEQUENCE type to decode each record as.

column_normalization.description: Bronze/raw column-name normalization with configurable case folding. The ONLY switch as of v1.4.0 -- the legacy boolean source_config.normalize_column_names is REMOVED and is rejected by onboarding validation with a migration message, not ignored. `enabled` defaults to false. The character normalization (trim, replace [^A-Za-z0-9_] with _, collapse repeated _, strip edge _) is ALWAYS applied deterministically -- only the case fold is configurable -- and collision detection is ALWAYS performed on the lowercased form, since Unity Catalog resolves column names case-insensitively. See ingestion/column_normalization.py.

schema_config_path.description: Path to an external JSON/YAML schema_config file (or a directory, resolved to its latest file) -- explicit type mapping, nullability documentation, Unity Catalog column comments, and source-to-target renames. See docs/28_ingestion_schema_config.md and ingestion/schema_config.py.

source_description.description: Free text, unvalidated -- becomes the target Delta table's COMMENT.

allOf.$comment: SCD3 is transformation_flows-only -- always a hard error on an ingestion_flows entry.

dataflow_id.description: Dependency-ordering label only -- the real data dependency is source_inputs[].table.

source_description.description: Free text describing what this flow produces; becomes the target table's Unity Catalog COMMENT, exactly as it does for an ingestion flow. Present in the Python validator's ALLOWED_TRANSFORMATION_FLOW_KEYS since the v2 schema but omitted here, so a spec setting it passed validate_spec and was then rejected by this schema's additionalProperties:false -- the two gates disagreed. Added in v1.7.4 to close that drift.

transformation_sql.$comment: Syntax/plan-validated live via EXPLAIN against a real Spark session -- this schema only checks it is a non-empty string.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

reconciliationDatasetConfig.description: Shared shape for reconciliation source_config and each target_configs[] entry.

type.description: Default: 'table'. Reconciliation is supported for Delta tables ONLY as of v1.3.0 -- read a file/sink location into a Delta table first, then reconcile against that table.

table.description: Required when type == 'table' (or type omitted, defaulting to 'table').

task_run_id_column.description: Optional. The column on this side carrying the producing pipeline/job run id. When the task_run_id job parameter is set, this side's read is narrowed to that run's rows. Reconciliation is triggered-only as of v1.4.0 (recon_mode is removed), so this narrowing is unconditional whenever both are configured. The framework's own materialized tables carry __framework_pipeline_run_id, which is the usual value. Absent means task_run_id stays correlation-only (the pre-v1.3.0 behaviour).

filter_condition.description: ${param}-substituted Spark SQL predicate, applied via .filter() right after read -- and after any task_run_id_column narrowing, so it can narrow further.

hash_precomputed.description: Default: false. Only valid when type == 'table'.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

reconciliationDatasetConfig.$comment: additionalProperties is deliberately NOT set here. This def is composed via allOf by reconciliationTargetConfig, which adds target_id/comparison_direction/append_target_table -- and a subschema's additionalProperties cannot see properties declared in a SIBLING allOf subschema, so closing it here rejected every valid target_config (and every reconciliation spec in flowx_testing/). Unknown keys are still rejected, by spec_validator.py's reject_unknown_keys against ALLOWED_RECONCILIATION_SOURCE_CONFIG_KEYS / ALLOWED_RECONCILIATION_TARGET_CONFIG_KEYS. Fixed in v1.7.4.

append_target_table.description: Required when comparison_direction is 'source_to_target' or 'both' (i.e. whenever it is not exactly 'target_to_source').

reconciliationTargetConfig.$comment: unevaluatedProperties (NOT additionalProperties) is what closes this composed def. additionalProperties only sees properties declared in its OWN subschema, so setting it on either allOf branch rejects the other branch's keys -- putting it on the base def rejected target_id/comparison_direction/append_target_table, and putting it on the target branch rejected type/table/read_mode/hash_precomputed. unevaluatedProperties evaluates after all allOf branches and therefore sees the union. Fixed in v1.7.4.

reconciliation_id.description: Also the key for reconciliation_run_log restartability.

dataflow_group_id.description: Which dataflow group's Lakeflow pipeline this reconciliation flow is registered into. Omit to inherit the spec's own top-level dataflow_group_id (the common case, and the pre-v1.5.0 behaviour); name a different group to register the flow inside THAT group's pipeline update instead. REQUIRED when execution_mode is 'pipeline' or 'pipeline_audit_only' (V-CYC-6): a group-less flow has no pipeline to be registered into. Persisted to reconciliation_flow_spec.dataflow_group_id.

execution_mode.description: Default: 'job' -- runs as a 05_reconciliation_engine.py job task, exactly as today; MUST stay the default because four DABs resources already run recon tasks against onboarded rows, and 'pipeline' as a default would run those flows twice per cycle. 'pipeline': registers this flow inside this dataflow group's Lakeflow pipeline update as a third flow type -- L3+L4 published comparison datasets AND the L5 heal (append-back) lane; requires dataflow_group_id (V-CYC-6) and an append-only source producer (V-CYC-7). 'pipeline_audit_only': registers L3+L4 only -- the comparison, metrics and dq_config expectations run in-pipeline, but healing stays in job mode; the landing zone if a foreach_batch_sink handler cannot read a pipeline dataset, and the correct setting for a recon flow whose source is static. See onboarding_spec_full_reference.md and docs/07_reconciliation_engine.md.

publish_schema.description: Schema (within the hosting pipeline's own catalog) where this flow's recon__<reconciliation_id>__<target_id>__classified / __metrics / __mismatch datasets are published. Default: the hosting pipeline's own schema. Only meaningful when execution_mode is 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only' -- REJECTED ON PRESENCE when execution_mode is 'job' (a job-mode flow produces none of those datasets), via reject_mode_incompatible_keys in spec_validator.py.

dq_config.description: Expectations attached to this flow's one-row recon__<reconciliation_id>__<target_id>__metrics dataset, e.g. {"rules": [{"rule_id": "no_value_drift", "expression": "value_drift_count = 0", "action": "fail"}]}. The first declarative way a reconciliation threshold can fail a pipeline update -- additive, and does NOT repurpose error_handling.on_failure, which keeps its exception-level try/except meaning. action 'quarantine' is REJECTED here (there is nothing to quarantine on a one-row metrics table). Only meaningful when execution_mode is 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only' -- REJECTED ON PRESENCE when execution_mode is 'job' (a job task has no dataset to attach expectations to).

two_tier_verification.description: Default: true. Phase 1 compares a cheap per-side (row_count, bit_xor of __framework_hash_key, bit_xor of __framework_hash_value) fingerprint and short-circuits the whole comparison when both sides match; Phase 2 (the full hash-key join and column-level discrepancy mapping) runs only when Phase 1 reports a difference. Set false to always run Phase 2 -- see reconciliation/matcher.py for the XOR-fold's documented pair-cancellation property.

logging_config.description: Per-flow log-write gates. BREAKING CHANGE in v1.7.3: both now default to FALSE (they defaulted to true through v1.7.2) -- reconciliation is SILENT BY DEFAULT and auditing is opt-in. A flow that omits logging_config entirely writes NO reconciliation_run_log, reconciliation_result or reconciliation_mismatch_log rows, and in pipeline mode registers NEITHER the recon__*__metrics NOR the recon__*__mismatch dataset. To keep pre-v1.7.3 behaviour, set both flags to true explicitly. Overridden at run time by the recon_run_log_capture / recon_mismatch_log job parameters (tri-state; unset defers to this block) -- see notebooks/05_reconciliation/05_reconciliation_engine.py. Contract: run_log_capture gates reconciliation_run_log AND reconciliation_result, and in pipeline mode whether the recon__*__metrics dataset is registered at all; mismatch_log_capture gates reconciliation_mismatch_log and the recon__*__mismatch dataset. Both false == reconciliation persists ONLY to its business target tables; the run's job/pipeline state is then the only failure signal. Rejected combinations -- and note that since v1.7.3 both are reachable by OMITTING logging_config, not only by writing false: dq_config.rules while run_log_capture resolves false (the expectations attach to __metrics, which would not exist), and execution_mode=pipeline_audit_only with both flags resolving false (the flow would register compute with no output). Either way the fix is to set run_log_capture: true explicitly.

run_log_capture.description: Default: false since v1.7.3 (was true through v1.7.2). When true, gates reconciliation_run_log AND reconciliation_result rows and, in pipeline mode, registration of the recon__*__metrics dataset. Must be set true explicitly when the flow declares dq_config.rules.

mismatch_log_capture.description: Default: false since v1.7.3 (was true through v1.7.2). When true, gates reconciliation_mismatch_log rows and, in pipeline mode, registration of the recon__*__mismatch dataset.

target_configs.description: A LIST, not a single object -- one flow can compare its source against multiple, independently-configured targets.

compare_columns.description: Empty/omitted forces hash-equality to always pass (key-presence-only matching).

transform_sql.$comment: Must read FROM _reconciliation_unmatched_records. ${param}-substituted then syntax/plan-validated live via EXPLAIN, same as transformation_sql.

^_.description: Author comment; ignored by the framework.

enabled.description: Active/inactive flag. Defaults to true when omitted.

mode.description: 'triggered' (default): served by notebooks/08_observability/08_dlt_observability_engine.py, the bounded post-update export for one pipeline. 'continuous': served by notebooks/06_observability_streaming/06_event_log_otel_streaming_pipeline.py, the always-on export streaming N event-log tables. A destination is served by exactly one of the two.

timeout_ms.description: OTLP_CONSUMER only. Merged into retry_config_json.timeout_ms by upsert_observability_config.

protocol.$comment: Only OTLP_HTTP_JSON is implemented by destination_dispatcher.py today -- see docs/25_dlt_observability_module.md Extending section.

resource_attributes.description: Extra/override OTel resource attributes merged in by destination_dispatcher.py::merge_resource_attributes immediately before dispatch.

observabilityEventLogTables.description: Continuous mode only, and REQUIRED there. Fully-qualified catalog.schema.event_log_table names -- each a real Unity Catalog Delta table one source pipeline publishes its own event log to. Streamed and unioned by the continuous observability pipeline.

observabilityCredentialRef.description: 'env:<VAR_NAME>' or 'secret:<scope>:<key>' -- see destination_dispatcher.py::resolve_credential. Literal secret values never validate against this pattern.
